correctness.rationale: The graph and entire neighborhood face poset are exhaustively constructed from explicit quadratic residues. A deterministic 1711-pair matching on all 3468 nonempty simplices is verified acyclic by a complete topological sort of 15300 oriented cover incidences. The resulting CW model has one 0-cell, five 2-cells and forty 3-cells. Exact signed gradient-path computation reconstructs its 5-by-40 boundary. A 4-minor is -1, a 5-minor is -3, and modular ranks are four modulo 3 and five modulo 2; hence Smith diagonal 1,1,1,1,3 over Z. As pi_2 of the 2-skeleton wedge of five 2-spheres is Z^5, the integer matrix classifies the attaching maps and proves M(Z/3,2) wedge 35 S^3. A second independent neighborhood-face construction and modular simplicial boundary calculation over F2, F3 and F5 agrees. Explicit code and matrix artifacts reproduce each nonstandard computation. No claim is made for other graph orders.

originality.rationale: The compared statements have materially different mathematical scope. Matsushita (arXiv:1210.2803; published primary MSC 55Q05) supplies the graph-theoretic description of fundamental groups of neighborhood complexes, not the integral higher-dimensional attaching maps of the order-17 Paley graph. Kahle (arXiv:math/0512077) proves probabilistic asymptotic results for random graphs. Shukla (arXiv:1802.04526) treats maximum degree at most three or four-regular circulants, while the target graph is eight-regular. Graph data tabulations record the Paley-17 intersection parameters, not its integral neighborhood-complex homotopy. Searches using the graph, Hom-complex, conference-graph and Ramsey aliases did not identify a statement implying the explicit Moore summand or 35 three-spheres. Search incompleteness is a real residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent exact Paley17 neighborhood-complex homotopy computation may exist outside the inspected or indexed literature.

value.rationale: The Paley17 graph is a canonical and uniquely important order-17 Ramsey-extremal strongly regular graph, not an arbitrary induced subgraph chosen after computation. Its ordinary Lovasz neighborhood complex is the natural homotopy invariant associated with graph-coloring obstructions. The newly computed integral Z/3 class in degree two is a genuine Moore-space obstruction: it cannot occur in any wedge of spheres, and disappears from ordinary rational or mod-two Betti numbers. The exact 35 remaining degree-three spheres and attaching-degree certificate are intrinsic and potentially reusable in comparing homotopy theories of conference graphs; no unsupported broader theorem or claim of practical impact is needed.
